title: Support Escalation ↔ Incident Comms Alignment (Status Page + Customer Threads)
author: Rafael Mendes
body:
## Purpose
This page defines a single, consistent approach for **customer-facing communication** when an issue is (a) a Support escalation, (b) an Engineering/SRE investigation, or (c) a formal incident with public status-page updates.

It answers:
- **When do we post to the status page vs. keep comms in tickets/threads?**
- **What can we safely share externally and what must stay internal/restricted?**
- **How does Support mirror incident updates into customer threads** (Zendesk/Jira customer tickets, email threads, shared Slack Connect channels) without drifting from the canonical incident timeline?

This is an *alignment document*; it does not replace the escalation playbook, incident process, or customer comms templates. Use those pages for definitions, SLAs, and exact copy blocks.

---

## Guiding principles
1) **One canonical narrative.** The incident channel (and incident ticket, if created) is the source of truth. Support mirrors that narrative; Support does not invent new technical hypotheses or ETAs.
2) **Fast acknowledgement, measured specificity.** Early comms should be timely, factual, and scoped (what we know / what we’re doing / when we’ll update next).
3) **No speculation.** Share confirmed symptoms and mitigation steps. Avoid guessing root cause, blast radius, or timelines.
4) **Minimize customer toil.** If we already have enough signals internally, don’t over-request logs. If we need customer data, request the minimum required fields.
5) **Protect customer confidentiality.** Never mention other customers, internal dashboards, hostnames, or restricted security details.
6) **Consistency across tiers.** Enterprise customers may get higher cadence and more direct comms, but messaging must remain aligned to the same facts.

---

## Definitions (quick)
- **Support escalation:** Support asks Eng/SRE/Security for help on a customer-impacting issue but it may not meet “incident” criteria.
- **Incident:** A declared operational event following the oncall/incident process (incident channel created, roles assigned, regular updates).
- **Status page update:** Public communication visible to many customers; requires higher confidence, careful wording, and coordinated cadence.

See the escalation playbook severity matrix for formal definitions and examples.

---

## Decision: when to post a status page update
Use the matrix below. When in doubt, ask SRE Oncall (or Incident Commander if an incident is declared).

### Status page posting criteria (minimum bar)
Post a status page update when **any** of the following are true:
- **Multi-customer impact** is confirmed or strongly indicated (not isolated to a single org/project) AND symptoms are customer-visible (e.g., elevated 5xx, widespread timeouts, streaming disconnect rate spikes).
- **Material impact to a core API surface** (chat/generate/embeddings) in a region for > ~10 minutes with no immediate mitigation.
- **A critical platform capability is degraded** (auth/login for multiple customers, control plane outage, quota enforcement outage causing broad failures).
- **Security incident comms required** (only when Security Incident Coordinator approves external messaging).

Do **not** post a status update for:
- Single-customer issues, including Private deployment outages isolated to one tenant/VPC/on-prem cluster.
- Known-issues where the workaround is clear and impact is limited (e.g., customer misconfigured retries causing 429 loops), unless metrics indicate platform-wide degradation.
- Unconfirmed reports without supporting telemetry.

### Ownership of the decision
- **SRE Oncall / Incident Commander**: final decision to post/update/resolve on status page.
- **Support Lead on the case**: responsible for ensuring affected customers receive mirrored updates and are not surprised by status page wording.

---

## Comms cadence and “who says what”
### Canonical update loop
1) **Incident channel update** (IC/Comms Lead posts)
2) **Status page update** (if applicable; typically by Comms Lead or IC)
3) **Support mirror update** into:
   - Customer ticket(s)
   - Customer email thread(s)
   - Shared Slack Connect channel(s) (if used)

Support mirrors the same:
- symptom statement
- mitigation status
- next update time
- any customer actions (only if confirmed and safe)

Support should avoid:
- internal hypotheses
- unapproved mitigation steps
- internal links (dashboards/runbooks)

### Recommended cadence (default)
If an incident is declared:
- **Initial acknowledgement**: within 15 minutes of incident declaration (status page + support mirror if customers already reporting)
- **During active mitigation**: every 30–60 minutes, or sooner on major changes
- **Monitoring after mitigation**: every 60–120 minutes until stable
- **Resolution**: when metrics confirm recovery and rollback risk is low

If it is a Support escalation (no incident):
- Follow SLA tables by tier, but keep **customer threads aligned** to Engineering’s investigation rhythm.
- If Engineering/SRE expects >60 minutes without a meaningful update, Support should set expectations explicitly (“no change yet; continuing investigation; next update by …”).

---

## What we can share externally (safe-to-share rules)
### Safe-to-share (generally OK)
- High-level symptoms: “increased error rates,” “elevated latency,” “intermittent streaming disconnects”
- Scope: impacted region(s) and product surface (“Hosted API in eu-west”, “Dedicated capacity in us-east”) if confirmed
- Customer impact framing: “some requests may fail,” “responses may be delayed,” “streaming may disconnect”
- What we’re doing (high-level): “investigating,” “applying mitigation,” “rolling back,” “failing over”
- Customer mitigations that are validated and documented in Known Issues pages (e.g., client-side retry/backoff guidance, streaming reconnect patterns, temporary region failover guidance when supported)

### Not safe-to-share (do not include in customer comms)
- Other customers’ identifiers, volumes, or timelines (“Customer X is also impacted”)
- Internal service names, hostnames, pod/node details, oncall tooling screenshots
- Root cause speculation (“likely due to kernel regression…”) before confirmed
- Security details (vulnerability specifics, exploitation indicators) unless Security Incident Coordinator approves wording
- Precise ETAs unless IC explicitly approves (“back in 10 minutes”)

### Handling restricted customer incidents (Private / regulated / security-sensitive)
- Mark threads and tickets as **restricted** when they include customer identifiers, network diagrams, audit logs, SSO configs, or security artifacts.
- Use redaction-friendly summaries in shared channels.
- If a status page update is needed for a security event, Security owns external wording; Support mirrors only the approved text.

---

## Support mirroring: required behavior
When an incident exists and a customer is impacted (or plausibly impacted):
1) **Link the incident reference internally** (incident channel + incident ticket ID, if any).
2) In the customer thread, post **the same facts** as the latest incident update.
3) Always include:
   - “We are investigating” / “Mitigation in progress” / “Mitigation applied; monitoring”
   - customer-visible symptom summary
   - next update time
4) If the customer asks for RCA:
   - Acknowledge and set expectation (RCA availability depends on tier/process)
   - Do not promise a date unless provided by IC/Support leadership

### Mirroring checklist (copy/paste)
- [ ] Confirm whether an incident is declared.
- [ ] Confirm status page state: Investigating / Identified / Monitoring / Resolved.
- [ ] Copy the latest approved external summary (status page text if present; otherwise incident comms lead summary).
- [ ] Add customer-specific context only if it is confirmed (e.g., “We see elevated errors for your org in eu-west”).
- [ ] Provide next update time.

---

## Status page wording alignment rules
If a status page update exists:
- Support should **reuse the same wording** as closely as possible.
- If the customer’s experience differs from the status page summary (e.g., they are 100% down but status says “intermittent”):
  - Do not contradict the status page in public.
  - Escalate internally to IC/Comms Lead to refine scope.
  - In the customer thread, say: “We’re seeing broader degradation; we’re validating the scope and will update accordingly.”

If no status page update exists:
- Support should communicate using approved templates and keep statements scoped to that customer until multi-customer impact is confirmed.

---

## Examples
### Example A: Elevated 5xx in a region (Hosted)
- Trigger: multiple customers report failures; telemetry confirms 5xx spike in eu-west.
- Action:
  - SRE declares incident.
  - Status page: Investigating.
  - Support mirrors into all active impacted tickets.
- Customer-safe phrasing:
  - “We’re investigating elevated 5xx errors affecting some requests to the Hosted API in eu-west. Next update by 10:30 UTC.”

### Example B: Single Dedicated customer latency spike
- Trigger: one Dedicated pool experiencing peak-hour latency; other pools healthy.
- Action:
  - Support escalation to Dedicated/SRE; no status page update.
  - Support comms remain customer-specific, offer validated mitigations (autoscaling policy review, temporary routing/fallback if configured).

### Example C: Private SSO/SAML login failures
- Trigger: isolated to one Private/VPC deployment after IdP change.
- Action:
  - Escalate to Private Deployments + Security as needed.
  - No status page update (single tenant).
  - Mark thread restricted if configs/logs shared.

---

## Roles & responsibilities (RACI)
**Incident Commander (IC)**
- Owns incident timeline, decisions, internal cadence, and approves externally shared facts.

**Comms Lead (if assigned)**
- Drafts status page updates and internal summaries for Support to mirror.

**SRE Oncall**
- Determines whether an issue meets incident criteria; advises on status page posting.

**Support Lead (case owner)**
- Ensures customer threads are updated, consistent, and aligned with incident comms.
- Consolidates customer questions and routes them back to IC/Eng owners.

**Customer Success (CSM/TAM)**
- Maintains relationship context, ensures comms tone is appropriate, escalates expectation mismatches.

**Security Incident Coordinator (if applicable)**
- Owns external wording for security-related events.

---

## Escalation: when Support should push for incident declaration
Support should request incident declaration (or re-evaluation) when:
- Multiple distinct customers report the same failure mode in the same region/model/version window.
- There is clear telemetry evidence of platform-wide degradation.
- A customer is asking for a status page post and there is credible broader impact.

Support should *not* request incident declaration solely to meet an individual customer’s comms preference if impact remains isolated and mitigations are in progress.

---

## Templates (short-form snippets)
Use the full templates page for longer variants. These are “quick mirror” snippets.

### Investigating (no status page yet)
“We’re investigating the issue you’re seeing and have engaged our engineering/on-call team. At the moment we believe the impact may be isolated, but we’re actively validating scope. Next update by <time>.”

### Mirror a status page update
“Mirroring our current status update: <paste status page text>. Next update by <time>.”

### Mitigation applied / monitoring
“We’ve applied a mitigation and are monitoring to confirm recovery. You may still see intermittent impact while systems stabilize. Next update by <time>.”

### Resolution
“We’ve confirmed recovery and are continuing to monitor. If you’re still seeing impact, please share recent request IDs and timestamps so we can investigate your specific traces.”

---

## Operational notes
- **Do not paste internal incident channel transcripts** into customer threads.
- If Support receives new customer-impact evidence (request IDs, precise timestamps, region/model), post it back into the incident channel using the required fields checklist.
- When an incident closes, ensure:
  - impacted tickets are updated with the resolution statement
  - any temporary mitigations are documented (Known Issues page if it is a recurring pattern)
  - follow-up expectations (RCA availability) are set correctly by tier

---
